hints: Look at the scale bar under the capillary. It says 7 µm, so that printed length on the page equals 7 µm in real life. Grab a ruler and measure that bar in mm.
Remember magnification = image size divided by actual size, but both must be in the same units. How will you convert your mm measurement into µm before dividing by 7 µm?
walkthrough:
**Measure the image size**

Lovely and simple to start. Use a ruler to measure the length of the 7 µm scale bar on the page.

You should get about $35 \text{ mm}$. This is your image size.

**Convert to the same units**

We cannot divide mm by µm directly, so let's change mm into µm. Remember:
$$1 \text{ mm} = 1000 \text{ µm}$$
So:
$$35 \text{ mm} \times 1000 = 35,000 \text{ µm}$$

**Apply the magnification formula**

Now use the golden rule for microscopy:
$$\text{magnification} = \frac{\text{image size}}{\text{actual size}}$$
Put your numbers in:
$$\text{magnification} = \frac{35,000 \text{ µm}}{7 \text{ µm}} = 5000$$
So the drawing is $\times 5000$. Well done, that is option D.

options.A: Too small. x200 would give an image size of only 1.4 mm for a 7 µm structure, much smaller than the drawing.
options.B: Too small. This value suggests a measuring or unit conversion error, as the bar clearly measures about 35 mm on the page.
options.C: Ten times too small. This is a common slip if you mix up mm and cm or miss a zero when converting to µm.
options.D: Correct. A 35 mm image divided by a 7 µm real size (35,000 µm / 7 µm) gives exactly x5000.
